title: Russian Su-35 Shot Down 42km From Front — MoD Fake Maps Misled Pilot — OSINT Geolocated July 14 2026
narrative:
On July 8, 2026, the Ukrainian Air Force shot down a Russian Su-35 multirole fighter jet in the eastern sector of the front. On July 9, Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps released video footage showing smoke rising from the crash site near the village of Mostky in Luhansk Region. OSINT analysts from GeoConfirmed and Ukraine Control Map geolocated the wreckage to approximately 49°22'47.6"N, 38°31'12.9"E — roughly 42 kilometers from the active front line.

The critical finding from UA Control Map: the pilot likely believed he was operating at a safe distance from the combat zone because he was navigating using official maps published by the Russian Defense Ministry. Those maps routinely depict territories as fully captured by Russian forces even though they remain under Ukrainian control. "They probably thought they were farther from the front, relying on Russian maps, once again hoisted by their own MoD's petard," analysts wrote.

Russian Z-channels confirmed the loss and reported the pilot ejected and was evacuated. The Russian Ministry of Defense has not commented on the shootdown. The Insider verified the geolocated coordinates; satellite imagery of the area shows a burning object consistent with the reported crash site.
analysis:
The Su-35 is one of Russia's most capable and expensive fighter aircraft (estimated unit cost ~$85M). Losing one to a navigation error caused by one's own military's cartographic inflation is a structural failure, not a tactical one.

This connects to a documented pattern: the July 3 OSINT analysis of command-post maps shown to Putin at a meeting with Defense Ministry officials, which inflated Russian-controlled territory by approximately 1,900 km² compared to what DeepState and ISW mapping projects showed at the same date. That analysis was about strategic-level deception (maps shown to the commander-in-chief). The Su-35 incident is the tactical-level consequence: a pilot trusting the same inflated maps and flying into a kill zone 42 km deeper than he believed.

The chain of evidence:
1. Russian MoD maps show territory as captured (documented by DeepState, ISW, and the July 3 command-post analysis).
2. A Su-35 pilot uses these maps for mission planning/navigation.
3. The pilot enters Ukrainian-controlled airspace believing it is Russian-controlled.
4. Ukrainian air defenses engage and shoot down the aircraft.
5. OSINT analysts geolocate the crash site and identify the map-discrepancy as the causal factor.

The MoD's silence is itself evidentiary. Unlike the Z-channel community (which confirmed the loss), the official MoD has not acknowledged the shootdown — consistent with a pattern of suppressing losses that would expose institutional failures (in this case, the cartographic inflation that caused the loss).

Satellite imagery verification: The Insider confirmed the geolocated coordinates show a burning object consistent with the crash site. This is the physical evidence layer that contradicts any potential Russian denial of the shootdown.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: The "hoisted by their own petard" story: Russia's institutional cartographic inflation — documented at the command-post level in the July 3 analysis — has now produced a concrete, geolocated, satellite-verified fatal consequence. The Su-35 pilot trusted MoD maps that showed Ukrainian-controlled territory as Russian-controlled, flew 42 km into a kill zone, and was shot down. The MoD's silence on the loss is the institutional response to an embarrassment it cannot explain without acknowledging the map-inflation problem. This is a structural-failure story, not a tactical-loss story — the same map-inflation that deceived Putin in the command post also deceived the pilot in the cockpit. Beat-distinct from the July 3 command-post maps story: that was about strategic-level deception; this is about the tactical-level consequence with a satellite-verified crash site.
